rationale: C20 is the expressly referenced July 20, 1948 proclamation and supplies the child’s concrete drafting framework. The child reproduces its statutory recitals and closely adapts its numbered registration provisions: age limits and registration dates, appearance before registration officials or local boards, delayed registration for absence or circumstances beyond control, familiarity with regulations, calls for official assistance, and employer cooperation. The principal adaptation is substitution of the Canal Zone and updated dates for the jurisdictions and dates in C20. C19 contains closely related regulatory language, while C21 reuses the same registration machinery for specialist registration, but neither is as direct a template as C20.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The registration of male citizens of the United States who shall have attained the eighteenth anniversary ... and who shall have not attained the twenty-sixth anniversary ... shall take place in the Canal Zone between the hours of 8:00 A.M. and 5:00 P.M.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The registration of male citizens of the United States and other male persons ... who shall have attained the eighteenth anniversary ... and who shall have not attained the twenty-sixth anniversary ... shall take place ... between the hours of 8:00 A.M. and 5:00 P.M.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely copies C20’s first operative provision while narrowing the covered population and substituting the Canal Zone.

shared_material.child_excerpt: is required to and shall ... present himself for and submit to registration before a duly designated registration official or selective service local board having jurisdiction in the area in which he has his permanent home or in which he may happen to be
shared_material.parent_excerpt: is required to and shall ... present himself for and submit to registration before a duly designated registration official or selective service local board having jurisdiction in the area in which he has his permanent home or in which he may happen to be
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, nearly verbatim operative language governing the place and manner of registration.

shared_material.child_excerpt: A person subject to registration may register after the day or days fixed for registration in case he is prevented ... by circumstances beyond his control or because he is not present in the Canal Zone
shared_material.parent_excerpt: A person subject to registration may register after the day or days fixed for registration in case he is prevented ... by circumstances beyond his control or because he is not present in any of the several States ... [and listed jurisdictions]
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves C20’s exception and subsequent-entry machinery, replacing the earlier list of jurisdictions with the Canal Zone.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Every person subject to registration is required to familiarize himself with the rules and regulations governing registration and to comply therewith.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Every person subject to registration is required to familiarize himself with the rules and regulations governing registration and to comply therewith.
shared_material.explanation: The provision is reproduced verbatim in the same operative sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I urge all employers and Government agencies of all kindsFederal and localto give those under their charge sufficient time in which to fulfill the obligations of registration
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I urge all employers and Government agencies of all kinds—Federal, State, territorial and local—to give those under their charge sufficient time in which to fulfill the obligations of registration
shared_material.explanation: The child directly adapts C20’s concluding cooperation clause to the Canal Zone’s governmental setting.
